name: Dhu al-Rumma
bio: Ghaylan ibn Uqba, known as Dhu al-Rumma, lived in the desert in Umayyad times and often visited al-Yamama and Basra. Mayya of the Minqar figures in his love poetry, which follows the tracks of gazelles and wild asses as closely as it does the traces of her camps. Al-Zirikli records Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’s judgement that a line of poets beginning with Imru al-Qays ended with him. He died in 117 AH (735 CE), in Isfahan according to one account and in the desert according to another.
